data.body:
MERGED — but this ticket stays OPEN, because its last AC is an operator action I cannot perform.

Gerrit change 1650 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1650) merged with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, and landed on origin/main as 5a3ad479f0 (Gerrit rebased it server-side onto c9234694e0).

WHAT IS TRUE AS OF MERGE:
- AC1 (distinguishable without host shell) — CODE LANDED. observability.sh 4e emits review_interrupts_bound_exceeded and review_interrupts_signal_unavailable as separate metrics; monitoring_autodeploy.tf declares rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded and rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable, each carrying only its own remediation. EFFECTIVE ONLY AFTER APPLY (see below).
- AC2 (signal-unavailable stays prompt) — LANDED. Its alarm keeps period=900, evaluation_periods=1, datapoints_to_alarm=1, threshold=0, GreaterThanThreshold, notBreaching. Identical to the pre-split cadence, so the split changed no sensitivity in either direction.
- AC3 (dimensions agree both sides) — LANDED. No dimension anywhere: the split is by metric NAME, so the monitoring_s4b.tf silent-unmatch hazard is structurally impossible here rather than merely avoided. A test asserts no --dimensions is ever passed.
- AC4 (rolled-up total still published) — LANDED. review_interrupts is published unchanged, so pre-split history stays readable and any future third reason is still counted; it is no longer ALARMED, so a single interrupt cannot double-page.
- AC5 (proven by an automated test) — LANDED. tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py drives the real observability.sh over a synthetic unit journal. It includes the piranha case as a named test: four firings that are ALL bound-exceeded leave review_interrupts_signal_unavailable at 0 — the exact discrimination 7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9 needed SSM shell access for. Re-verified on the landed tree at 5a3ad479f0: 14 passed, terraform fmt -check and terraform validate both clean.
- AC6 (applied, not merely merged, and recorded) — NOT SATISFIED. THIS IS WHAT KEEPS THE TICKET OPEN.

OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED — terraform apply in infra/terraform.

Until that apply runs, NOTHING about alarming has actually changed on the account, and the intermediate state is worth understanding before someone reads a dashboard and draws the wrong conclusion:
- The host probe starts publishing the two new metrics as soon as the new observability.sh reaches the box via autodeploy — that half needs no apply.
- But the ALARMS are still the old single rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts on the rolled-up metric. So between merge and apply, behaviour is exactly as before: an interrupt pages once, without a reason. Nothing regresses, nothing improves.
- After apply, the old alarm is REPLACED by the two new ones. Expect the old alarm name to disappear from the console; that is intended, not an accident, and it is the only destructive part of the plan.
- The two new alarms will read INSUFFICIENT_DATA until their first datapoint, then settle to OK via treat_missing_data = notBreaching.

I did not run terraform apply and deliberately did not attempt to: this ticket is observability-only and I have no mandate to mutate live infrastructure. Please re-open this comment thread with the apply output (or a plan diff) once it has run, and then AC6 is satisfiable and the ticket can close.

COORDINATION NOTE: bug 2dc7 (affluent-conveyable-dromedary, Gerrit 1648, marker counters recounting on rotation) was still open when 1650 landed. The two changes are disjoint by construction — 1648 rewrites the negative-delta clamp INSIDE the publish helpers, this change touches only the comment block, the offset-file declarations and the call sites — but 1648 now needs a rebase over 5a3ad479f0. Its clamp change will apply to the two new reason counters automatically, since they go through the same helper.
